title: Rearrange K Substrings to Form Target String
summary: Given two strings s and t , both of which are anagrams of each other, and an integer k , determine if it is possible to split string s into k equal-sized substrings, rearrange these substrings in any order, and concatenate them to form string t .
statement: Given two strings s and t , both of which are anagrams of each other, and an integer k , determine if it is possible to split string s into k equal-sized substrings, rearrange these substrings in any order, and concatenate them to form string t . Return true if this is possible, otherwise return false. An anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, using all the original letters exactly once. A substring is a contiguous non-empty sequence of characters within a string.
constraints: s and t are equal-length lowercase anagrams of length up to 200,000; k divides their length.
Split both strings at the same k equal-size block boundaries.
Return whether reordering whole blocks from s, without editing inside a block, can form t.
hints: Only block order may change, so the multiset of exact block strings is invariant.
Slice both strings with block length len(s)/k and compare frequency maps.
Count every aligned block in s and t; equality of the two counters is the answer.
Equal multisets can be paired and reordered to match target order; any differing block count makes construction impossible.
editorial: Equal multisets can be paired and reordered to match target order; any differing block count makes construction impossible.

tests.explanation: The source blocks ab and cd can be swapped to form target blocks cd and ab.
Both strings contain exactly the length-two blocks aa, bb, and cc.
